# Data Cleaning 

```{r}
#| message: false

# install.packages(tidyverse)
# install.packages("dplyr")
# install.packages("knitr")
# install.packages("tinytable")
# install.packages("readr")

library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(tinytable)
library(readr)
```

```{r}
# Read in raw data 

raw_data <- read.csv("Commute_Data_Database.csv")

raw_data
```

```{r}
# Renaming columns that will not be dropped in next step 

commute_relabeled_cols <- raw_data |>
  rename(
    Geography = GEO, 
    Gender = Gender..3., 
    Mode = Main.mode.of.commuting..11A., 
    Immigrant_Status = Immigrant.status.and.period.of.immigration..11., 
    Count = VALUE
  )

names(commute_relabeled_cols) # Confirming renaming worked as planned
```

```{r}
# Setting which modes of transportation will be kept in this dataset 
# Filtering out "Driver with 1 or more workers", "Passenger with 2 or more
# workers", and "Sustainable transportation" as these include duplicates 
# with the modes kept

modes_keep <- c("Car, truck or van", "Public transit", "Active transportation", 
                "Other method")

# Filtering out unecessary columns to keep and ensuring that the "Immigrant 
# Status" column does not include duplicates by only looking at "Total -
# Immigrant status and period of immigration"
commute_clean <- commute_relabeled_cols |> 
  filter(
    Immigrant_Status == "Total - Immigrant status and period of immigration", 
    Mode %in% modes_keep
  ) |> 
  select(Geography, Gender, Mode, Count)

# Test to ensure that output is correct 
# (Should be 13 provinces x 2 genders x 4 modes of transportation)
stopifnot(nrow(commute_clean) == 104) 
```

```{r}
commute_clean <- commute_clean |> 
  mutate(Count = as.integer(Count))

commute_clean
```

```{r}
commute_clean <- commute_clean |> 
  arrange(Geography, Gender, Mode)

commute_clean
```

```{r}
# Adding a "Total" column to allow percentage calculation for each row of the 
# data frame 

commute_clean <- commute_clean |> 
  group_by(Geography, Gender) |> 
  mutate(Total = sum(Count)) |> 
  ungroup()

commute_clean
```

```{r}
# Adding a "Percentage" column to match with simulated data visualization and 
# plan for EDA

commute_clean <- commute_clean |> 
  mutate(Percent = Count / Total * 100)

commute_clean
```

```{r}
# Creating easy-to-read table from commute_clean for easy viewing

commute_clean |> 
  tt() |> 
  format_tt(j = c("Count", "Total"), digits = 0, num_fmt = "decimal", 
            num_mark_big = ",") |>
  format_tt(j = "Percent", fn = \(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", x)) |>
  style_tt(j = 1:6, align = "lllrrr")
```

```{r}
# Test to ensure "Count" = integer column & does not include negative values
stopifnot(
  "Count must be an integer column" = is.integer(commute_clean$Count),
  "Count has negative values"       = all(commute_clean$Count >= 0)
)

# Test to ensure there are no missing values in dataset
stopifnot("Data contains missing values" = !anyNA(commute_clean))

# Test to ensure there is no blank text strings in dataset
stopifnot(
  "Blank text found" = all(
    commute_clean |> 
      select(where(is.character)) |> 
      map_lgl(\(x) all(str_trim(x) !=""))
  )
)
```

```{r}
write_csv(commute_clean, "Cleaned_Commute.csv")
```

```{r}
# Testing that categories (Mode, Gender, and Geography) align with expected n

mode_counts   <- count(commute_clean, Mode)
gender_counts <- count(commute_clean, Gender)
geography_counts <- count(commute_clean, Geography)

stopifnot(
  "Expected exactly 4 modes" = nrow(mode_counts) == 4,
  "Each mode should have 26 rows (13 provinces x 2 genders)" = 
    all(mode_counts$n == 26),
  "Modes are not the expected four" = setequal(
    mode_counts$Mode,
    c("Car, truck or van", "Public transit", "Active transportation", 
      "Other method")
  ),
  "Expected exactly 2 genders" = nrow(gender_counts) == 2,
  "Each gender should have 52 rows (13 provinces x 4 modes)" = 
    all(gender_counts$n == 52),
  "Gender values are not Men+ and Women+" = 
    setequal(gender_counts$Gender, c("Men+", "Women+")),
  "Expected exactly 13 provinces and territories" = 
    n_distinct(commute_clean$Geography) == 13
)
```

```{r}
# Beginning with head and tail of data to see the top 

clean_data <- read.csv("Cleaned_Commute.csv")

head(clean_data)
tail(clean_data)
```

```{r}
# Random slice of 6 rows from data frame. Seed used to ensure reproducibility

set.seed(723)

clean_data |>
slice_sample(n = 6)
```

```{r}
clean_data |>
  glimpse()
```

```{r}
# Creating a summary table that is grouped by Mode & Gender to create summary 
# statistics that are meaningful, rather than mixing four different modes of 
# transportation (which would not create meaningful or comparable statistics)

clean_data |>
  group_by(Mode, Gender) |>
  summarise( 
    n = n(),
    national_pct = sum(Count) / sum(Total) * 100, 
    min_pct = min(Percent),
    median_pct = median(Percent), 
    mean_pct = mean(Percent), 
    max_pct = max(Percent), 
    .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
  rename(
    "Mode" = Mode, 
    "Gender" = Gender, 
    "National (%)" = national_pct, 
    "Mean (%)" = mean_pct,
    "Median (%)" = median_pct, 
    "Minimum (%)" = min_pct, 
    "Maximum (%)" = max_pct
  ) |> 
  tt() |> 
  format_tt(j = 3:8, digits = 1, num_fmt = "decimal") |>
  style_tt(j = 1:8, align = "llrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
# Transit share by province, men vs. women
transit_eda <- commute_clean |> 
  filter(Mode == "Public transit")

nrow(transit_eda) # should be 26
```
```{r}
ggplot(transit_eda, aes(x = Percent, y = fct_reorder(Geography, Percent), 
                        colour = Gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Women+" = "#6CCED9", "Men+" = "#EC9C3E")) +
  labs(
    title = "What Does the Distribution of Transit Users Look Like Across 
    Canadian Provinces and Territories?", 
    x = "Commuters using public transit (%)", 
    y = "Canadian Provinces & Territories") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```

```{r}
# Visualizing gender gap (Women+ minus Men+) by province 

gap <- gap |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(gap > 0, "Women+ higher", "Men+ higher"))

ggplot(gap, aes(x = gap, y = fct_reorder(Geography, gap), fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Women+ higher" = "#6CCED9", "Men+ higher" = "#EC9C3E")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Is There a Gender Gap in Canadian Transit Use?", 
    x = "Gap in percentage points (Women+ minus Men+)",
    y = "Canadian Provinces & Territories",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```
```{r}
# Creating a list of province/territory abbreviations for following graph's 
# labels (to reduce clutter)

prov_abbr <- c(
  "Newfoundland and Labrador" = "NL", 
  "Prince Edward Island" = "PEI", 
  "Nova Scotia" = "NS", 
  "New Brunswick" = "NB", 
  "Quebec" = "QC", 
  "Ontario" = "ON", 
  "Manitoba" = "MB", 
  "Saskatchewan" = "SK", 
  "Alberta" = "AB", 
  "British Columbia" = "BC", 
  "Yukon" = "YT", 
  "Northwest Territories" = "NWT", 
  "Nunavut" = "NU"
)
```

```{r}
# Does a place's size relate to its share?
ggplot(transit_eda, aes(x = Total, y = Percent, colour = Gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) prov_abbr[x]) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = unname(prov_abbr[Geography])),
                size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Women+" = "#6CCED9", "Men+" = "#EC9C3E")) + 
  labs(
    title = "Does a Province/Territory Size Relate to its Share of Commuters?", 
    x = "Total commuters (log scale)", 
    y = "Commuters using public transit (%)", 
    colour = "Gender"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```
